chunks.title: Photosynthesis basics
chunks.text: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. Chlorophyll in thylakoid membranes captures photons so plants can build sugar. Plants make food from sunlight through this process. Фотосинтез и хлорофилл запасают энергию в глюкозе. Так работает фотосинтез: хлорофилл ловит свет.

chunks.title: Spaced repetition
chunks.text: Spaced repetition schedules reviews along the forgetting curve. A Leitner interval schedule lengthens gaps after successful recall so memory decays more slowly.

chunks.title: Retrieval practice
chunks.text: Retrieval practice, also called the testing effect, strengthens memory by asking learners to perform free recall of facts instead of rereading notes.

chunks.title: Active recall flashcards
chunks.text: Active recall flashcards force a learner to produce an answer from the card front, including cloze deletion prompts, before the back is revealed.

chunks.title: Bloom taxonomy
chunks.text: Bloom taxonomy orders learning objectives from remember and understand up through analyze, evaluate, and create. These taxonomy levels describe cognitive demand.

chunks.title: Cognitive load
chunks.text: Working memory has limited slots, so extraneous cognitive load should be reduced during explanations. Germane load supports schema building.

chunks.title: Interleaving practice
chunks.text: Interleaving mixes different problem types in one practice session instead of blocked practice of a single type. A mixed problem set improves later discrimination.

chunks.title: Elaborative interrogation
chunks.text: Elaborative interrogation asks why a fact is true so learners form a prior knowledge link. Why-questioning connects new ideas to what the learner already knows.
